subject: Project Atlas: physical media authentication & controlled update cadence
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@astrahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@astrahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Project Atlas: physical media authentication & controlled update cadence

Jonas,

Thanks for taking this early. We're standing up an air-gapped VI (vendor-isolated) cluster for Project Atlas and need a concrete plan from Redwood for how images and updates will be delivered, signed, and validated on-site. Key asks from our compliance team:

- Proof the image was produced by Redwood (cryptographic signature anchored to an HSM/KMS).
- Manifest with image digest, build id, timestamp, and signer identity.
- Chain-of-custody guidance for physical media shipments (tamper seals, dual-operator handoff).
- Update cadence options: regular monthly maintenance vs emergency security hotfixes (expect a 48-hour SLA for critical CVEs).
- What audit artifacts will we get (signing logs, key rotation records, install verification logs)?

Attached is a brief spec (atlas_requirements.pdf) from our security ops team. Can you confirm Redwood's approach and supply a runbook + verification tool we can run at install time? We'd like to kick off a short tech review next week.

—Alex
IT Security, Astra Health

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@astrahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Project Atlas: physical media authentication & controlled update cadence

Alex — thanks, and appreciate the spec. High level answer first: yes — we support HSM-anchored signing for offline artifacts, a signed JSON manifest per image, and an offline verifier binary your operators run before install.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) Tech review meeting (30m) — Thu 2027-03-31 or Fri 2027-04-01.
2) We'll provide a draft runbook + manifest schema for review (will attach signed-manifest-schema.json and runbook_v1.md).
3) Define monthly maintenance windows vs emergency patch process (we propose monthly scheduled updates + a documented 48-hour critical patch path that includes staged verification).

I'll loop in Marissa and Neha for the operational checklist and chain-of-custody items. Can you share preferred shipment carriers and whether site personnel require background-checked couriers? Also confirm if your auditors require signed DocuSign receipts on handoff.

Thanks — jonas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 26 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Atlas media-auth checklist and verifier design

All — sketching the checklist we should present. Keeping things tight and prescriptive for an air-gapped customer: 

Signing & manifest
- Build pipeline produces image + sha256 digest.
- Signing system: HSM-backed ECDSA P-384 key (YubiHSM / cloud-HSM) with key-id and key-policy recorded.
- Manifest (signed-manifest-schema.json): { release_id, image_digest, build_tags, build_timestamp, signer_key_id, signature, allowed_kv_cache_version } (we'll document exact JSON schema).
- Signature algorithm: SHA-256 digest then ECDSA-P384 signing; verify using provided public cert chain.

Physical delivery & chain-of-custody
- Media: encrypted NVMe in tamper-evident enclosure; external tamper seal with serial.
- Dual-operator handoff: on-ship and on-receive operators sign manifest (printed + QR + signature block).
- QR contains manifest URL fingerprint + signature blob (for easy operator validation before connecting to air-gapped host).

On-site verification tool
- Lightweight verifier binary (static) that expects: image file, manifest.json, public-cert.pem.
- Verifier checks digest, signature chain, and prints a human-readable report with a signed install acceptance token (so operators can attach to install ticket).

Update cadence and emergency flow
- Default cadence: monthly maintenance window (configurable).
- Emergency critical patch: 48-hour response — produce signed emergency image, secure transfer to pre-approved courier, remote approval (DocuSign or signed email) OK for handoff if physical sign-off impossible.
- Rollback: signed previous-image manifests retained and verifiable; verifier supports revert confirmation.

Audit artifacts we can provide
- Signing audit: time-stamped HSM logs (key usage events), signing request ids.
- Build provenance: immutable build metadata and commit hash.
- Install verification logs: verifier output (text + signed accept token).

Attachments: signed-manifest-schema.json (draft), staging-test-plan.xlsx (validation checklist).

I'll draft a short runbook for install and a P0 emergency playbook. Dev — can you capture the verifier's CLI args and expected exit codes so we can include in the runbook?

—Marissa
Sr. PM, Private Deployments

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@astrahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@astrahealth.com>, IT Security <secops@astrahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Project Atlas: physical media authentication & controlled update cadence

Jonas / Marissa — this looks good and aligns with our auditors' expectations. A few follow-ups before the tech review:

1) Can you confirm whether the HSM audit stream can be exported (redacted) for our SOC2 report? We don't need key material, but need key usage timestamps, signer key-id, and request ids.
2) For emergency patch courier: we need a template chain-of-custody form (DocuSign acceptable) that both the shipper and site operator sign.
3) We'd like a short demo of the verifier on a staging VM before handoff. Date request: can we do the demo during the tech review slot on 2027-03-31?

If you can attach the runbook draft and the verifier CLI help ahead of the call that would be helpful. Also please include an example of the signed-manifest.json with real-looking fields (not prod keys).

Thanks — Alex

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Project Atlas: physical media authentication & controlled update cadence

Alex — great questions. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- HSM audit stream: yes, we can export a redacted usage log showing timestamps, signer key-id, and signing request ids. We'll redact any key material. We'll provide retention policy and a sample export format in the runbook.
- Chain-of-custody: we'll include a DocuSign template for two-tier signoff (shipper + on-site lead) and an optional courier background-check checkbox. Link to draft: https://docusign.com/XYZ-Agreement-Atlas
- Demo: confirmed for 2027-03-31 11:00AM PT — we'll run the verifier on a staging VM and walk through a canned emergency patch flow.

Deliverables before the call (we will attach to the calendar invite):
- runbook_v1.md (install + verification steps)
- signed-manifest-schema.json (example manifest + sample signed blob)
- staging-test-plan.xlsx (verification checklist)

After the call we'll finalize the monthly cadence and emergency SLA language for the contract. If auditors request, we'll also coordinate export of sample signing logs to Astra's security mailbox.

Thanks — jonas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
